{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  tests:
    name: Build and test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      # Underworld.csproj targets net9.0 and the test project targets net10.0.
      # SDK 10 builds both; SDK 8 builds neither.
      - name: Set up .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: '10.0.x'

      # Godot itself is not needed: Godot.NET.Sdk and GodotSharp restore from NuGet.
      - name: Build
        run: dotnet build Underworld.csproj

      # The test project is deliberately outside Underworld.sln, so name it.
      # These never load Godot, and the game-data tests return early when the
      # .SYS files are absent.
      - name: Unit tests
        # Only the font tests. The rest of the suite reads save fixtures from
        # ../UW2GOG, which is proprietary game data this runner has no licence to
        # carry, so 30 of its 177 tests fail here through no fault of the code. Making
        # those skip is worth doing and belongs on issue #60, where the maintainer
        # already offered to decide the CI layout; it is not this branch's to take.
        run: |
          dotnet test tests/Underworld.Save.Tests/Underworld.Save.Tests.csproj \
            --verbosity normal \
            --filter "FullyQualifiedName~SysFont|FullyQualifiedName~InstallationValidator|FullyQualifiedName~SceneFontWiring"

  render:
    name: Font render test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Set up .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          # Underworld.csproj targets net9.0, so its runtimeconfig asks for
          # Microsoft.NETCore.App 9.0.0 with LatestMinor roll-forward, which does not cross
          # to 10. A 10 SDK builds it happily but Godot cannot host it, and the failure is
          # silent: CoreCLR never starts, so no test writes a line and the log holds only
          # shutdown noise. Both are needed here.
          dotnet-version: |
            9.0.x
            10.0.x

      - name: Install xvfb
        run: |
          # Mesa too: xvfb supplies an X display but no GPU, so the software GL driver
          # is what actually rasterises the render test.
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y xvfb libgl1-mesa-dri libglx-mesa0

      # The mono build, because the render test is C# and calls SysFontBuilder.
      - name: Fetch Godot 4.3 mono
        run: |
          curl -sL -o godot.zip \
            https://github.com/godotengine/godot-builds/releases/download/4.3-stable/Godot_v4.3-stable_mono_linux_x86_64.zip
          unzip -q godot.zip
          echo "GODOT=$PWD/Godot_v4.3-stable_mono_linux_x86_64/Godot_v4.3-stable_mono_linux.x86_64" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Build
        run: dotnet build Underworld.csproj

      # A fresh checkout has no .godot directory, and Godot cannot run a scene until it
      # has imported the project once. Without this every scene dies before it prints
      # anything, which reads as "produced no verdict".
      - name: Import the project
        run: |
          chmod +x "$GODOT"
          xvfb-run -a "$GODOT" --headless --path . --import || true

      # A real driver under xvfb, never --headless: the render test compares pixels, and
      # headless returns dummy values from the RenderingServer.
      #
      # Every scene is run, not just the render test. The exit status is not trusted:
      # Godot 4.3 mono can fault on shutdown after Quit(), so each test prints a verdict
      # line and this harness keys off that. A run that prints no verdict is a failure,
      # because it died before deciding.
      #
      # SKIP is expected here and is not a failure: several of these need the shipped game
      # data, which CI has no licence to carry. They report SKIP and start protecting the
      # branch the moment game data is available. Until then CI proves those scenes load and
      # run, not that their assertions hold.
      - name: Godot tests
        run: |
          chmod +x "$GODOT"
          rc=0
          for scene in font_render_test font_placement_test cursor_placement_test font_boot_test font_failure_test \
                       font_resize_test font_demo_boot_test launcher_validation_test ordinal_fit_test; do
            out="/tmp/$scene.log"
            timeout 180 xvfb-run -a "$GODOT" --rendering-driver opengl3 \
              --path . "res://tests/godot/$scene.tscn" > "$out" 2>&1 || true
            verdict=$(grep -m1 '^GODOT-TEST-VERDICT ' "$out" || true)
            if [ -z "$verdict" ]; then
              # Print the START of the log, not the end. Godot's real error happens during
              # startup, while the tail is filled with allocator and static-string
              # diagnostics it emits on every shutdown. Tailing hid a missing runtime.
              echo "::error::$scene produced no verdict"
              head -40 "$out"
              echo "  ... matching lines ..."
              grep -iE 'hostfxr|coreclr|dotnet|assembly|runtime' "$out" | head -10 || true
              rc=1
            else
              echo "$scene: $verdict"
              case "$verdict" in
                *" PASS"*) ;;
                *" SKIP"*) echo "::notice::$scene skipped, no game data" ;;
                *) echo "::error::$scene failed"; tail -30 "$out"; rc=1 ;;
              esac
            fi
          done
          exit $rc
",
  "rationale": "Add explicit job timeouts (timeout-minutes: 5) to both jobs. The repository has representative successful-duration history (5 recent successful runs completing in ~1-2 minutes). The experiment evidence (batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) demonstrates measured elapsed-time savings of 26.8% when adding a 5-minute timeout to a similar workflow job. This minimal change bounds runaway consumption without affecting build/test coverage, as the timeout provides ample headroom over observed durations.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}

The user wants me to analyze the provided CI workflow and evidence to propose an evidence-supported optimization. I need to return a JSON object with decision (APPLY or NO_CHANGE), workflow_yaml (updated workflow if APPLY), rationale, and evidence_ids.

Let me analyze the workflow first:

The workflow has two jobs:
1. `tests` - Build and test (runs on ubuntu-latest)
2. `render` - Font render test (runs on ubuntu-latest)

Both jobs run on every pull_request and push to main.

Looking at the evidence provided, I have several experiment examples and pattern catalogues. The most relevant ones seem to be:

1. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT - shows adding timeout-minutes to a job (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508)
2. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST - shows enabling fail-fast for matrix jobs (multiple experiments)
3. P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE - cancel superseded runs
4. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE - cache dependency downloads

Let me check the workflow for applicability:

1. **Custom Timeout (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT)**: The workflow currently has no timeout-minutes set. The evidence shows adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to a job. This could be applicable to prevent runaway jobs. The pattern requires "Representative successful-duration history exists" - we have some CI history showing successful runs.

2. **Fail Fast (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST)**: The workflow doesn't use matrix strategy, so this doesn't apply directly.

3. **Cancel Stale (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE)**: Could apply to cancel superseded runs on the same branch/PR. The workflow runs on pull_request and push to main.

3. **Cache (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE)**: The workflow uses `dotnet build` and `dotnet test`. There's no explicit caching of NuGet packages. The setup-dotnet action might have some caching, but we could add explicit caching.

Let me look at the workflow more carefully:

- The `tests` job: checks out, sets up .NET 10, builds, runs tests
- The `render` job: checks out, sets up .NET 9 and 10, installs xvfb and mesa, fetches Godot, builds, imports project, runs Godot tests

For the `render` job, there's a lot of setup (installing xvfb, mesa, downloading Godot). This could benefit from caching.

However, the evidence for P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is about dependency caching. The pattern says "Choose dependency download state rather than unchecked build outputs" and "Keep installation and all required tests".

Looking at the experiment for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508), it shows adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to a job that runs ESLint, Typecheck, etc. The median elapsed seconds went from 41 to 30 (26.8% savings).

For our workflow, both jobs could benefit from timeouts. The `render` job especially has a loop with `timeout 180` for each scene, but the job itself has no overall timeout.

The CI history shows runs completing in about 1-2 minutes (from created_at to updated_at). For example, the latest run: created 21:21:20, updated 21:22:13 = ~53 seconds. Another: 20:13:18 to 20:14:35 = ~77 seconds.

So a timeout of 5-10 minutes would be reasonable with plenty of headroom.

The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern has preconditions: "Representative successful-duration history exists" - we have 5 successful runs in history.

The evidence IDs available:
- experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 (for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT)
- experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-4bb0552aeb09c242 (for P-LIT-FAIL-FAST)
- experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-6e84419c6d8620c3 (for P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST)
- experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-c4031f01d86b1653 (for P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST)
- experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-b6e04fef7ef24997 (for P-LIT-FAIL-FAST)

The most directly applicable is P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT with the experiment showing measured savings on a fork.

I should also consider P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE for canceling superseded runs on pull_request. The workflow runs on pull_request and push to main. For pull_request, if someone pushes new commits, the previous run could be canceled. This is a common optimization.

But the evidence for P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is from the pattern catalogue (simulation estimate), not from the experiment examples. The experiment examples are for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT and P-LIT-FAIL-FAST.

The instruction says "Use only supported evidence IDs; APPLY requires at least one." The evidence IDs are the document_ids from the evidence array.

Let me check: the evidence array has 5 items with document_ids:
1. experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT)
2. experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-4bb0552aeb09c242 (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST)
3. experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-6e84419c6d8620c3 (P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST)
4. experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-c4031f01d86b1653 (P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST)
5. experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-b6e04fef7ef24997 (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST)

The pattern catalogue has patterns but those are not "evidence IDs" in the same sense - the instruction says "Use only supported evidence IDs" referring to the evidence array.

So I should use the experiment evidence IDs.

The most applicable is P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) because:
1. The workflow has no timeouts
2. The experiment shows measured savings (26.8% elapsed time reduction)
3. The workflow has representative successful-duration history (5 successful runs)
4. Adding timeout-minutes is a minimal change that preserves all checks

I'll propose adding timeout-minutes to both jobs. Based on the CI history (runs complete in ~1-2 minutes), a timeout of 5 minutes gives plenty of headroom (similar to the experiment which used 5 minutes for a ~41 second job).

Let me create the updated workflow YAML.

Current workflow:
```yaml
name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  tests:
    name: Build and test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      ...

  render:
    name: Font render test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      ...
```

Updated workflow with timeout-minutes: 5 for both jobs:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  tests:
    name: Build and test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      ...

  render:
    name: Font render test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      ...
```

This is a minimal change, preserves all build and test coverage, and is supported by the experiment evidence.

I'll use evidence ID: experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508

Decision: APPLY
